objectives.text: Given the type and application of an AC generator, DESCRIBE the operating characteristics of that generator including methods of voltage production, advantages of each type, and methods for paralleling.

enabling.text: STATE the purpose of the following components of an AC generator:
Given the speed of rotation and number of poles, CALCULATE the frequency output of an AC generator.
LIST the three losses found in an AC generator.
Given the prime mover input and generator output, DETERMINE the efficiency of an AC generator.
DESCRIBE the bases behind the kW and current ratings of an AC generator.
DESCRIBE the conditions that must be met prior to paralleling two AC generators including consequences of not meeting these conditions.
DESCRIBE the difference between a stationary field, rotating armature AC generator and a rotating field, stationary armature AC generator.
EXPLAIN the differences between a wye-connected and delta-connected AC generator including advantages and disadvantages of each type.

passages.quote: The field in an AC generator consists of coils of conductors within the generator that receive a voltage from a source (called excitation) and produce a magnetic flux.
The armature is the part of an AC generator in which voltage is produced.
The prime mover is the component that is used to drive the AC generator.
The rotor of an AC generator is the rotating component of the generator
The stator of an AC generator is the part that is stationary
Slip rings are electrical connections that are used to transfer power to and from the rotor of an AC generator
The magnitude of AC voltage generated by an AC generator is dependent on the field strength and speed of the rotor.
The frequency of the generated voltage is dependent on the number of field poles and the speed at which the generator is operated
Efficiency of an AC generator is the ratio of the useful power output to the total power input.
The combination of these make up what is known as the internal resistance, which causes a loss in an AC generator.
Power (kW) ratings of an AC generator are based on the ability of the prime mover to overcome generator losses and the ability of the machine to dissipate the internally generated heat.
Three conditions must be met prior to paralleling (or synchronizing) AC
If the voltages of the two AC generators are not equal, one of the AC generators could be picked up as a reactive load to the other AC generator.
A mismatch in frequencies of the two AC generators will cause the generator with the lower frequency to be picked up as a load on the other generator
The worst case mismatch would be 180° out of phase, resulting in an opposing voltage between the two generators of twice the output voltage.
Phase matching is accomplished through the use of a synchroscope
Minimize VAR loading

passages.quote: Small AC generators usually have a stationary field and a rotating armature
armature type AC generator is used when large power generation is involved.
An advantage of the delta-connected AC generator is that if one phase becomes damaged or open, the remaining two phases can still deliver three-phase power.
An advantage of a wye-connected AC generator is that each phase only has to carry 57.7% of line voltage and, therefore, can be used for high voltage generation.
You can see that a delta-connected generator provides an increase in current, but no increase in voltage.

body.text: The magnetic flux in the field cuts the armature to produce a voltage.
The armature consists of many coils of wire large enough to carry the full-load current.

body.alt: A basic AC generator in cutaway, with the rotor, stator, field, slip rings, and output labeled.

body.text: The rotor is driven by the prime mover. It may be the armature or the field, depending on the type of generator.
Like the rotor, the stator may be the armature or the field.
Slip rings allow the output current and voltage to oscillate through positive and negative values, in the shape of a sine wave. A DC generator uses a commutator instead.

body.cap: Comparison of DC and AC Generator Outputs
body.alt: Two output waveforms: a DC generator with one polarity from a commutator, and an AC generator with a sine wave from slip rings.

body.text: Most generators are operated at a constant speed, so the generated voltage depends on field excitation.
f is frequency in Hz, P is the total number of poles, and N is rotor speed in rpm.
There are three losses in an AC generator:

items: Internal voltage drops, due to the internal resistance and impedance of the armature

body.text: Hysteresis losses occur when iron cores are subject to effects from a magnetic field. Rotating magnetic domains cause friction and heat.
Mechanical losses can be caused by bearing friction, brush friction, and air friction, called windage.
Efficiency = (Output / Input) x 100
Input and output power must be in the same units.

checks.x: The three losses are internal voltage drops, hysteresis losses, and mechanical losses.

body.text: Typical nameplate data includes speed, number of poles, frequency, number of phases, maximum supply voltage, capacity in KVA and kW at a specified power factor, armature and field current per phase, and maximum temperature rise.
The current rating of an AC generator is based on the insulation rating of the machine.

checks.x: Power (kW) ratings are based on the ability of the prime mover to overcome generator losses and the ability of the machine to dissipate the internally generated heat.

items: Their terminal voltages must be equal.
Their output voltages must be in phase.

o: 90° out of phase, with no opposing voltage

If DC field excitation is connected to the rotor, the stationary coils will have AC induced into them. This is a rotating field, stationary armature AC generator.

Its advantages: a load can be connected to the armature without moving contacts in the circuit, it is much easier to insulate stator fields than rotating fields, and much higher voltages and currents can be generated.

o: It cannot produce a sine wave

body.text: A three-phase generator has three equally-spaced windings and three output voltages, all 120° out of phase with one another.
In a delta connection, the windings are connected in series.

body.alt: Delta connection: three windings in a closed triangle, with lines A, B, and C from the corners.

body.text: The voltage between any two phases, called line voltage, is the same as the voltage generated in any one phase. The current in any line is √3 times the phase current.

body.alt: Delta-connected generator diagram labeled with equal phase and line voltages, and line currents larger than phase currents.

body.text: With one phase out, the capacity of the generator is reduced to 57.7% of what it was.
In a wye connection, one of the leads of each winding is connected, and the remaining three leads are connected to an external load.

body.alt: Wye connection: three windings joined at a neutral point, with lines A, B, and C from the outer ends.

body.text: Voltage between any two lines is 1.73 times any one phase voltage, while line currents are equal to phase currents.

body.cap: Characteristics of a Wye-Connected AC Generator
body.alt: Wye-connected generator diagram labeled with line voltages larger than phase voltages, and equal phase and line currents.

checks.q: What does a delta-connected generator provide?
o: An increase in voltage, but no increase in current
An increase in current, but no increase in voltage
An increase in both voltage and current
checks.x: A delta-connected generator provides an increase in current, but no increase in voltage.

checks.q: What is an advantage of a delta-connected AC generator?
o: It can still deliver three-phase power if one phase is open
Each phase carries 57.7% of line voltage
checks.x: If one phase becomes damaged or open, the remaining two phases can still deliver three-phase power, at reduced capacity.

checks.q: Why is a wye-connected AC generator suited to high voltage generation?
o: Each phase only has to carry 57.7% of line voltage
checks.x: Each phase only has to carry 57.7% of line voltage and, therefore, it can be used for high voltage generation.

summary.text: The field produces a magnetic flux, the armature is where output voltage is produced, and the prime mover drives the generator.
Frequency is found by multiplying the number of poles by the speed and dividing by 120.
Efficiency is found by dividing the output by the input and multiplying by 100.
To parallel AC generators, their terminal voltages and frequencies must be equal, and their output voltages must be in phase.
A rotating field, stationary armature generator can generate much higher voltages and currents.
A delta-connected generator can still deliver three-phase power with one phase open, and a wye-connected generator can be used for high voltage generation.
